1.note: If your language would not represent numbers in a form such as **eighth** and **second**, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [In month eight in year two of Darius]

Zechariah is using **the word of Yahweh came to Zechariah** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh communicated a message to Zechariah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke his message to Zechariah] or [Yahweh gave his message to Zechariah]

Zechariah is using the phrase **In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius** to introduce a new event in the story (in this case, the very beginning). Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

2.note: Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [was extremely angry]

3.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell them that Yahweh of Armies says this]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s relationship with him were a place that they had physically left and could physically come back to. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Be faithful to me again] or [Renew your commitment to me]

The term **the declaration of Yahweh of Armies** introduces a parenthetical affirmation of the source of this direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating the authoritative source of direct quotations in your language.

Here, **Return to me** introduces the first part of a possible condition. Yahweh will only do the thing in the second part, **and I will return to you**, if this condition happens. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [If you return to me, then I will return to you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his renewed favor toward the people were a physical movement back to them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will be favorable to you again] or [and I will bless you again]

4.note: The terms **evil ways** and **evil deeds** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [from all of your evil conduct]

Yahweh is speaking of how the ancestors lived as if that were a **way** or path that they were walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from your evil behavior]

Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what the former prophets told the ancestors to do and what the ancestors actually did. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, they did not hear, and they did not pay attention]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and told them that Yahweh of Armies had said to]

The terms **did not hear** and **did not pay attention** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [But they completely refused to obey me]

5.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the ancestors are dead. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Your fathers are no longer alive.]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the prophets also died. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And the prophets did not live forever either.]

6.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the mortality of the fathers and prophets and the enduring effect of God’s words and statutes. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, my words and my statutes]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that his words certainly did overtake the ancestors. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [they certainly overtook your fathers.]

Yahweh is speaking of **my words and my statutes** as if they were living things that could pursue and catch people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my words and my statutes, … did they not come true for your fathers]

The pronoun **they** refers to the ancestors, not to the words and statutes mentioned earlier in the verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And your ancestors repented and said]

The ancestors are speaking of how they lived as if that were a **way** or path that they were walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to how we behaved and according to what we did]

7.note: Zechariah is using the phrase **On the twenty-fourth day** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Both **twenty-fourth** and **eleventh** are ordinal numbers. If your language would not represent a number in a ordinal form, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [On day twenty-four of month eleven]

The phrase **in the second year** uses an ordinal number. If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **second**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year two of the reign of Darius]

Zechariah is using **the word of Yahweh came to Zechariah** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh communicated a message to Zechariah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke his message to Zechariah] or [Yahweh gave his message to Zechariah]

The word **saying** normally introduces something Yahweh said. Here it introduces what Zechariah saw in a vision, which he describes in his own words starting in the next verse. If it would be unnatural in your language to use a speech word to introduce a vision, you could use a phrase that introduces a report or account instead, and you should not mark the vision as a quotation. Alternate translation: [the prophet. This is what Yahweh showed him:] or [the prophet, and this is what happened:]

8.note: Zechariah is using the phrase **I saw in the night, and behold** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and I saw]

10.note: The terms **answered and said** together introduce a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.
The pronoun **These** refers to the horses and their riders that Yahweh sent to patrol the earth. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These horses and riders]

11.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the horse riders who had been patrolling the earth, described in verse 8. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the riders answered]

The terms **answered** and **said** together introduce a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.

The riders are speaking of **all of the earth** as if it were a living thing that could sit down and be quiet. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the peoples of the earth are peaceful and calm]

12.q: עַד־מָתַ֗י אַתָּה֙ לֹֽא־תְרַחֵ֣ם אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְ⁠אֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָעַ֔מְתָּה זֶ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה
12.note: The angel of Yahweh is using the question form to urgently plead with God to show mercy. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Please have compassion on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah with which you have been indignant these 70 years now!]

Here, **Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah** represents the people who live in those places. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [on the people of Jerusalem and the people of the cities of Judah]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **comfort**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [words that comforted him]

14.q: קְרָ֣א לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Proclaim that Yahweh of Armies says this]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [I have been very zealous for Jerusalem and for Zion]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **jealousy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [indeed very jealous]

15.note: Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And I am very, very angry]

The pronoun **I** is repeated for emphasis in both clauses. You could translate Yahweh’s emphasis with a phrase that conveys strong personal involvement in your language. Alternate translation: [I myself am angry…I myself was angry]

15.q: אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ קָצַ֣פְתִּי מְּעָ֔ט וְ⁠הֵ֖מָּה עָזְר֥וּ לְ⁠רָעָֽה
15.note: Yahweh uses the word **but** here to indicate a contrast between the limited extent of his anger and the excessive harm the nations inflicted. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for I was angry only a little, yet they made the harm far worse]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **the evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to do what was harmful]

16.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [Because of this]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his renewed favor toward Jerusalem were a physical journey back to the city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have again shown favor to Jerusalem with mercy] or [I have once again been gracious to Jerusalem]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **compassions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [while acting mercifully to her people]

The expression **My house will be built in her** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the people of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the people will build my house in her]

The expression **a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the builders. Alternate translation: [and the builders will stretch out a measuring line over Jerusalem]

A **measuring line** is a kind of rope or cord that builders stretch out to measure distances when constructing or planning a building or city. If your readers would not be familiar with what a measuring line is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and a measuring rope]

17.note: Here, **My cities** represents the people who live in those cities. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The people living in my cities]

There are three levels of quotation here. The angel of Yahweh is speaking to Zechariah (level 1) and telling him to proclaim a message (level 2), which itself quotes what Yahweh of Armies says (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there is not a third-level quotation.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **goodness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from good things]

18.note: Zechariah is using the phrase **And I lifted up my eyes and I saw** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Zechariah is using **And I lifted up my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I looked” or “I directed my attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I looked up] or [And I directed my gaze upward]

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and there I saw]

19.note: Here, **the horns** represents the military power of the nations that attacked God’s people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the powerful nations that scattered the people of Judah]

Here, **Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem** represents the people who lived in those nations and that city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of Judah, the people of Israel, and the people of Jerusalem]

21.note: The word **These** is used three times in this verse with two different referents. The first and third **these** refers to the craftsmen. The second **these** refers to the horns, that is, the powerful nations. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [are these craftsmen … These horns are the nations … And these craftsmen have come]

The angel is using **according to the mouth of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “so that.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the extent that]

The angel is using **has not lifted up his head** as a common expression of the culture to mean “no one was able to resist or act with confidence.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no one was able to resist them] or [no one dared to oppose them]

The term translated as **And** here indicates that what follows is the result or purpose of what came before. The craftsmen have come in order to terrify the nations that scattered Judah. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [So these have come to terrify them]

Here, **the horns of the nations** represents the military power of those nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the armies of the nations]

Here, **lifting up a horn** represents exercising aggressive military power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the ones using their military power against the land of Judah]

Here, **the land of Judah** represents the people who live there. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [against the people of Judah]
